subject.title: [Feature]: Scope Codex native hook relay spawns with per-tool hook matchers

question: Should OpenClaw add a public exact-tool-name scope contract across plugin hooks, trusted-tool policies, and Codex tool-result middleware to control native relay installation?
rationale: This changes compatibility-sensitive plugin API and security-policy routing, while unresolved choices include naming, tool aliases, dynamic-tool double dispatch, unscoped-union semantics, fallback behavior, and whether a resident relay architecture should be preferred.

options.title: Approve exact-name scope API
options.body: Add one typed exact-name scope field across all relevant registrations, with deterministic aggregation and safely escaped Codex matcher serialization.

options.title: Keep scoping internal
options.body: Expose no new plugin contract and derive relay scope only from existing owner-specific metadata where OpenClaw can prove complete coverage.

options.title: Defer to resident relay
options.body: Avoid expanding the SDK now and prioritize an in-process or resident relay design that removes per-call process spawning more generally.

recommendation.title: Approve exact-name scope API
recommendation.body: Add one typed exact-name scope field across all relevant registrations, with deterministic aggregation and safely escaped Codex matcher serialization.

likelyOwner.reason: The native relay implementation history makes this person the strongest available owner for the architecture and security-boundary decision.
